title: Smoked mackerel toast with warm plums

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Smoked mackerel, crème fraîche, horseradish sauce, honey and bread are all ordinary kitchen staples, with no factory-made sauces or mixes.

supermarket.reason: Every item is an everyday Tesco purchase at a normal price, and smoked mackerel is a cheap fish.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a small saucepan, a bowl, a fork and a toaster or grill, with simple stewing and mashing.

works.reason: The quantities suit four (250g mackerel and eight slices), the plums will soften nicely in 8 to 10 minutes with a little liquid, and the sweet-sour plums cut through the smoky fish.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is fair for stoning six plums, flaking the fish, mixing and toasting eight slices, and the ten-minute cook matches the plum step.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the water, lemon, watercress and chives, is used in the steps, and nothing extra appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Warm September plums are cooked into a compote that tops every slice, so they are a main element rather than a garnish, and a warm breakfast suits early autumn.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear and neighbourly, in British English, with no restaurant jargon or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oily fish, wholemeal toast, watercress and fruit make a filling breakfast of real food that is not sugar-led.
